name: Orkla India Ltd
title: Orkla India Ltd - 544595 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Spice deflation has bottomed: Q4 price uptick (~4% realisation) and chilli up 20-30%, but volume growth slowed to 2.2% in Q4 and no PLI income was booked in FY26 (FY25: INR 20.5 cr).

triggers.label: Spice price uptick, price hike ~4%
triggers.quote: we are seeing a recovery in spice prices, with quarter 4 showing an 6.5% uptick

triggers.label: Chilli inflation 20-30%
triggers.quote: Key spices such as chili and coriander have seen inflation of 20% to 30% and 10% to 15% respectively

triggers.label: Q4 volume growth only 2.2%
triggers.quote: our volume growth was 2.2% whereas we recorded a revenue growth of 6.2%

triggers.label: US trade inventory flush-out
triggers.quote: us having inventories of multiple tariff levels in the US. So we are looking at flushing those inventories out

guidance.quote: our goal is to continue to work towards a double-digit growth performance, and we are pretty confident that we will move towards that in the near -term
We do see that by 1st of January 2027, this project should be complete
We expect to take another round of price increases in quarter one of FY27

red_flags.label: Q4 volume growth 2.2% vs revenue 6.2%
red_flags.quote: our volume growth was 2.2% whereas we recorded a revenue growth of 6.2%

red_flags.label: No PLI income in FY26; scheme ends FY27
red_flags.quote: This is the first year that we've not recognized PLI

red_flags.label: Kerala share loss and distribution disruption
red_flags.quote: Kerala market was impacted due to internal sales restructuring project

evasions.quote: we don't put out guidance, so I will refrain from giving you specific guidance on, you know, where we expect our margins to be
I don't think we give guidances on how much is the split between pure and blended spices

summary.headline: Orkla India Q4 FY26 revenue from products grew 6.2% and EBITDA hit INR 100 crore at 16% margin, with no PLI income booked for FY26.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from sales of products grew 6.2% on volume growth of 2.2%, with price increases of roughly 4% starting in the quarter. Excluding Kerala, which was hit by distribution restructuring and LPG-linked HoReCa softness, domestic spices grew 11.1% on 6.5% volume growth. FY26 EBITDA was INR 424 crore (16.9% margin) with no PLI income; excluding PLI, EBITDA grew 12.4%. Management flagged West Asia freight costs, Project BOLT digital investments, and renewed spice inflation as near-term margin pressures.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Q4 spices revenue grew 6.1%; excluding Kerala, domestic spices grew 11.1% on 6.5% volume. Karnataka category share up 30 bps and Kerala down 50 bps (MAT March 2026); AP share stable.

segments.name: Convenience Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 6.4%, with Meals and Sweets both growing double digits; Breakfast was flat due to a temporary slowdown at two quick-commerce platforms under restructuring.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 5.1%. GCC (about 70% of international) grew 11.8% (about 11.5% per Q&A); North America was soft on US tariff-driven destocking.

segments.name: Domestic digital commerce
segments.commentary: Digital commerce grew 23% YoY in Q4 and 38% in FY26, now 8.7% of domestic revenue vs 6.6% last year; 38% of MTR Prakriti sales come from non-South markets, D2C repeat rate 21%.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit growth in the near term, but gave no formal guidance; it does not issue guidance.

Kerala distribution restructuring expected to weigh for at least two more quarters; full completion targeted by 1 January 2027, with one phase done, another by end-May 2026, and a final phase taking at least two quarters.
Another round of price increases planned in Q1 FY27, calibrated to input cost moves.
Gulf shipments expected to keep growing, with stocks adequate; US business to recover once tariff-level inventories are flushed.
FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme; PLI recognition depends on meeting CAGR thresholds, which management called difficult to predict.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing footprint of eight in-house facilities and 22 outsourced units; management said it will keep rationalising the footprint and outsourcing lower value-added categories.
Distribution: 679,000 retail touchpoints; Eastern route-to-market being re-architected into three segments (spices coverage, convenience food, standalone modern trade).
Project BOLT, a digital commerce programme with an external agency, launched in Q4 with investments that weighed on margin; no capex figure disclosed.
Fresh wet batter convenience range extended to Hyderabad, in addition to existing markets.
MTR Karam Gold chili powder and MTR Karam launched for AP and Telangana.
demand_pricing: Spice prices rose about 6.5% in Q4 from lows after nearly seven quarters of decline; chili inflation 20-30% and coriander 10-15%.
Q4 pricing contributed roughly 4 percentage points of revenue growth against 2.2% volume growth.
FY26 volume growth 5.9%, the highest in four years (from 1.8% in FY23).
Q4 EBITDA margin was hit by about 200 bps from higher freight (West Asia) and Project BOLT investment.
95% of raw materials sourced locally; freight surcharges and packaging/logistics costs rising.
Management said small players were exiting Gulf supply due to freight costs, which helps larger players like Orkla.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Kerala distribution restructuring weigh, and when did it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Project kicked off in Q4; two of three phases implemented, one more by end-May; impact expected for at least two more quarters, with full completion by 1 January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What growth to expect from exports given 70% GCC exposure, and is the US tariff issue behind?
qa_highlights.answer: Gulf grew about 11.5%, with double-digit growth in the last two quarters. US softness came from destocking across multiple tariff levels (50% down to 16-17%); the business should normalise once inventories are flushed.

qa_highlights.question: What inflation and blended price increase were taken, and are more planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 price increase roughly 4% (6.2% sales growth less 2.2% volume). Another round is planned for Q1 FY27, calibrated to input costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA growth is structural versus temporary (lower ad spend, mix)?
qa_highlights.answer: Around half of the ~250 bps EBITDA margin gain since FY24 came from raw material price declines; the other half from efficiencies, cost reduction, pricing and mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is digital commerce growth incremental household penetration or channel migration?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: reaching new households, including outside South India, while some migration is seen in Southern metro cities. Market-level split not shared.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth tonnage-based, and how does PLI work and what was recognised last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume is absolute tonnage across all categories. PLI (six-year scheme from FY22) was not recognised in FY26 due to CAGR thresholds missed after two years of deflation; FY25 recognised INR 20.5 crore; FY27 is the last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pure vs blended spices split and the convenience food exposure outside South?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices about 26% and blended about 39-40% of revenue. Outside South growth is mainly via digital commerce; Breakfast flatness attributed to two quick-commerce platforms restructuring.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin aspiration and can Eastern reach MTR margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said Eastern margins have improved since its 2021 acquisition, with convenience-food shift and cost programmes expected to lift them further, but gap to MTR remains.

risks_watch: Kerala volume and share (market share down 50 bps MAT March 2026) during the distribution transition through early 2027.
West Asia conflict: freight surcharges, port closures and transit delays affecting GCC supply, which is about 70% of international.
Spice and packaging input inflation returning; margin protection depends on calibrated price increases in Q1 FY27.
PLI income uncertain for FY27, the scheme's final year, after nil recognition in FY26.
US inventory destocking and tariff volatility; North America growth soft in Q4.
Digital commerce investments under Project BOLT and quick-commerce partner restructuring affecting Breakfast.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term fundamentals and volume momentum, but cautious on near-term Kerala, Gulf freight and input-cost pressures. Management declined to give margin or growth guidance and answered several questions only partially.
key_quotes: While Kerala remains a near -time headwind, the underlying performance across other markets reinforces our strategy of driving depth and building a strong regional franchise which continues to deliver resilient growth.
So we do expect that these near -term disruptions that have happened will not really impact us in a sharp way as we go ahead into the next few quarters.
We expect to take another round of price increases in quarter one of FY27.
The strong EBITDA performance was driven by effective pricing actions, operational efficiencies, and disciplined advertising promotional spends and cost optimization.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +7% YoY; +12.4% excluding PLI; margin +30 bps (100 bps ex-PLI)

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax before exceptional items (FY26)
Revenue from sales of products excl. PLI (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: cash conversion ~98% of EBITDA adjusted for TDS on dividends

growth.why: No formal guidance; management aspires to double-digit growth "in the near-term" with no capacity or order numbers behind it, while Q4 growth was 6.2% mostly from ~4pp pricing and only 2.2% volume, and the Kerala restructuring weighs for at least two more quarters.
